messages:
dylan: Quick sync — I ran the new 'bridge-sampler' split yesterday (canary run #42) on the rtx-pools. We separated prefill vs gen batching and turned on the kernel probe. Results look mixed, dumping the short trace below.

maya: link the trace? perf-bot should have a summary.

perf-bot: automated summary -> https://perf.internal/runs/42 (uploads: cpu/kern/hist, kv-stats.csv)

 dylan: raw snippet from the run (aggregated over 10m):
 ```
 phase     | avg_batch | tokens/s | p95_latency_ms | kv_hit_rate | kernel_pref_count
 prefill   | 42.3      | 18200    | 18             | 0.72        | cutlass: 62%, naive: 38%
 gen       | 6.7       | 520      | 342            | 0.48        | cutlass: 22%, naive: 78%
 overall   | -         | -       | -              | -           | kernel_probe_fallbacks: 210
 ```

maya: interesting — prefill throughput is up (nice) but gen p95 jumped a lot. kv_hit_rate on gen is low; looks like prefill batches are evicting the KV entries gen needs during warmup. Also kernel probe seems to be picking a faster prefill kernel that performs poorly on short gen sequences (fallbacks spike).

alex: my 2c: sounds like token budget/queue policy tuning is needed. proposal:
 - lower prefill token_budget_target so prefill batches are slightly smaller (encourage fewer large evictions)
 - raise decode priority in the queue (prefer small gen batches under 12 tokens)
 - add hysteresis to kernel_probe (don't flip kernels until delta > 20% over 30s)

sophia: agree on hysteresis. also flag: streaming clients will see worse p95 if gen gets deprioritized too much. need a canary that has 2x streaming traffic share.

alex: config diff I'm suggesting (pseudo):
 ```json
 {
   "bridge_sampler": {
     "prefill": { "token_budget_target": 8 },
     "gen": { "min_priority_tokens": 1, "priority_threshold": 12 },
     "kernel_probe": { "delta_pct_threshold": 0.2, "probe_window_s": 30 }
   }
 }
 ```

maya: also add a KV sticky tweak: keep top-3 prefix entries pinned for 5s after a decode to reduce eviction churn between prefill->gen. small memory cost but should help hit rate.

perf-bot: quick numbers from a previous test with token_budget_target=10 + sticky_kv=5s -> gen p95 dropped from 340ms to 190ms, kv_hit_rate up from 0.41 to 0.63 (same pool).

 dylan: plan: run A/B canary across two hosts:
 - control: current (token_budget_target=12, kernel_probe default)
 - experiment: token_budget_target=8, kernel_probe delta=0.2, sticky_kv=5s, decode priority threshold=12
 I'll schedule for the 22:00 slot and post short-lived dashboards. can people watch tokenflow, kv-warmup, kernel-fallback counters?

 maya: :thumbsup: I'll watch dashboards and set an alert for kernel_probe_fallbacks > 50/min and gen_p95 > 250ms.

 sophia: I'll simulate streaming-heavy traffic against the canary and run long-context traces. if we see regressions rollback ASAP.

 alex: also add a small log marker on scheduler side so we can correlate prefill batch sizes -> eviction events (eg. `SCHED:prefill_evict=NN`).

 dylan: thanks — assigning follow-ups: alex (scheduler log), maya (alerts/dashboards), sophia (streaming sim), i'll roll canary. ping here when you see anomalies.

 maya: noted.

 perf-bot: scheduled canary -> https://perf.internal/canaries/bridge-sampler-42 (start=2387660000)
